prior_art.attribution: Mathlib's own proof is one line, `fib_of_odd <| odd_two_mul_add_one n`, and this kernel's route is exactly that shape once `Int.Odd` is stated via `natAbs` (F:int-odd) -- `fib_of_odd` was already proved (F:ml430-int-fib-of-odd-66560495); the new work is `Int.odd_two_mul_add_one`, proved by a case split on `n` reducing `2*n+1` to a Nat magnitude of the form `succ (mul 2 _)` in both signs, closed by a witness built from the ALREADY-DECLARED `second_supplementary.rs::two_mul_eq_add_self`/`odd_predicate` helpers (built for an unrelated quadratic-reciprocity modulus, reused unchanged here).

notes: A previous lane concluded this must stay open because our Nat.fib (tail-recursive accumulator) differs structurally from Mathlib's (Function.iterate over a pair). That reasoning does not apply here: the statement never evaluates Nat.fib's recursion, it only relates Int.fib (this kernel's own sign-extended construction, itself proved to agree with Nat.fib at odd indices via fib_of_odd) to Nat.fib at natAbs -- exactly the fact fib_of_odd already establishes, so composing it with 'the magnitude of 2*n+1 is odd' closes this theorem with no reference to fastFib/binaryRec or any other divergent construction. The earlier guidance that the oddness witness would be an Int-level existential (`∃ k, m = 2*k+1`) was also wrong: this kernel defines `Int.Odd n := Nat.Odd (natAbs n)` (parity.rs), so the real obligation was `Nat.Odd (natAbs (2*n+1))`, discharged by case-splitting n and observing both branches reduce natAbs(2*n+1) to the identical closed form `succ (mul 2 _)`.
